references.text: The same chapter describes the consequence of not cleansing oneself after contact with a dead body—the person defiles the Lord's tabernacle.
A parallel law concerning being cut off from the people for failing to celebrate Passover without valid reason, thereby dishonoring the Lord's sanctuary.
The principle of being cut off from the people for dishonoring the Lord's word and breaking His commandments.
Whoever eats the peace offering while unclean shall be cut off from their people—the same principle regarding uncleanness and exclusion applies.
The first occurrence of the expression 'cut off from their people' in connection with covenant breach.
The New Testament warns of even stricter punishment for those who profane the blood of God's Son and treat the Spirit of grace with contempt.
Failing to bring an offering to the tabernacle results in being cut off from the people—the same term 'nikreta' is used.
